🇾🇪 Ansar Allah closes in on Aden as Saudi Arabia is left on its own

While attention is on a possible new US war with Iran, Yemen's Ansar Allah is redrawing the map of West Asia.

Ansar Allah fighters have advanced to within 80 km of Aden, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-controlled puppet government, four military sources told Reuters on November 2. It's their deepest push toward the city since 2015, when they briefly entered it before being driven out.

The offensive took the Maqatirah mountain district between Aden and Taiz, giving Ansar Allah fire control over the main road between the two cities and a chance to outflank government forces along the mountains overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, has been encircled since early October, displacing more than 100,000 people. Ansar Allah has also struck Aden airport and the presidential palace.

Control of Bab el-Mandeb

In September, Ansar Allah seized the port of Mocha and Perim Island, which sits in the middle of the strait, after government troops withdrew. It now controls Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline.

According to The Wall Street Journal, shipping companies now email Ansar Allah asking for permission to pass. Captains declare their ships have no ties to the US, the UK, Israel or Saudi Arabia, and approved vessels receive seven-day transit permits. Ansar Allah says over 1,000 ships passed the strait in October, and that only Saudi shipping is targeted.

With Hormuz heavily restricted since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February, Bab el-Mandeb has become even more critical for global trade.

Meanwhile, Ansar Allah keeps striking Saudi oil facilities and airports with missiles and drones.

Saudi camp in crisis

The government's October 5 counteroffensive, launched to "liberate" all of Yemen, has collapsed, leaving thousands dead. President Rashad al-Alimi has since fired his longtime information minister and the commanders of the Taiz and Tur al-Bahah fronts, The Guardian reports. Southern forces, whose separatist leadership Riyadh crushed earlier this year, have said they will only fight to defend former South Yemen, the very forces Aden's defense depends on.

Washington isn't coming to help. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump twice in September urging US strikes, and Trump refused, offering only intelligence. Trump later said Ansar Allah had asked the US to stay out.

Riyadh has turned to the Mecca Alliance it signed with Turkey and Pakistan in August, which agreed in October to deploy forces to Saudi Arabia. Yemeni officials told AFP that hundreds of Syrian troops are already on both sides of the Saudi-Yemeni border, with up to 10,000 to follow under a deal signed by Syria's Ahmed al-Sharaa (a.k.a. Abu Mohammad al-Jolani) in Riyadh. Damascus denies sending troops, saying the deal covers training only.

Talks with Ansar Allah?

According to the WSJ, Riyadh has quietly reached out to Ansar Allah to ask what it would take to stop the attacks. The reported answer: $51 billion in compensation for years of bombing and blockade, plus recognition as Yemen's legitimate government. Saudi Arabia categorically denies the report, and a journalist close to Ansar Allah also disputed it.

If Riyadh does end up cutting a deal with Ansar Allah, and by extension Tehran, over Washington's head, it would be a sign that the US has lost its grip on one of the most strategic regions in the world.

🇵🇱 Who is the Krakow gunman?

The man who killed six people on Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday is Michał O., 24, from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski in southern Poland. Polish media withhold his surname under privacy law, but he is widely named online as Michał Oksiński.

Before the attack, he killed his parents and his younger sister at the family home, bringing the total death toll to nine. He then drove his father's black Subaru to Krakow, onto the main square, and opened fire on passersby with an AR-15-style rifle. Fifteen people were wounded, including two police officers. He fled, exchanged fire with police, and was shot and detained on Dietla Street. He survived thanks to body armor and remains in critical condition.

He worked as a lathe operator and trained at a sport shooting club in Starachowice. He held a permit for two guns, while his father legally owned 11. Neither had a criminal record. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said one theory is that he used his father's weapons, and police found many more guns and ammunition in the car.

Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz denied he ever served in the Polish army.

Far-right?

Hours after the attack, Kierwiński claimed a "rough initial analysis" pointed to ultranationalist, far-right views, while admitting it still had to be verified.

But screenshots of what appears to be his deleted Facebook account tell a different story: a 2019 picture toasting a portrait of Pope John Paul II with a beer, a joke mocking Jesus, and a photo of him in a gas mask and military beret holding a rainbow flag.

Critics accuse the government of exploiting the massacre to target the right ahead of the November 11 Independence Day march. Krakow's mayor Łukasz Gibała called him simply a madman.

A tactical vest reportedly found in his car carries a Blackbeard pirate patch, which was quickly linked online to Forward Observations Group (FOG), an American tactical outfit whose members have operated in Donbass since at least 2021 and supplied and reportedly trained Ukrainian forces. FOG uses its own variant of the Blackbeard flag as its logo.

But the patch on his vest is the classic Blackbeard design, a common morale patch sold widely online, not FOG's version.

So far, the picture that emerges is that of a typical US school shooter.

🎙 Iran’s Yousofi breaks world record, wins clean and jerk gold at World Championships

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian weightlifter Alireza Yousefi won the clean and jerk gold medal with a world-record lift and secured silver overall in the super-heavyweight category at the 2026 World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo, China.

The championships, the first qualifying event on the road to the 2026 Los Angeles Olympics, began on October 27 and concluded on November 8 with the super-heavyweight competition.
​
Ali Davoudi opened Iran’s campaign by lifting 206 kilograms in the snatch, earning bronze, while Yousefi placed fourth with 195 kilograms.
​
Yousefi then made his mark in the clean and jerk. After successfully lifting 253 kilograms in his first attempt, he failed to register 258 kilograms in his second. He succeeded with 263 kilograms in his final attempt, setting a world record and taking gold. His total of 458 kilograms earned him overall silver.
​
Davoudi lifted 246 kilograms in the clean and jerk but failed twice at 261 kilograms, finishing with 452 kilograms.
​
Iraq’s Ali Ammar won the overall title with 466 kilograms, while Armenia’s Varazdat Lalayan took bronze with 457 kilograms. Ammar also won snatch gold, while Lalayan secured snatch silver.
